<a id="limes.DefaultMaxTokenBytes"></a>

### limes.DefaultMaxTokenBytes

```go
const DefaultMaxTokenBytes = 16 << 10
```

DefaultMaxTokenBytes bounds the token a verifier will look at. A capability with a few dozen resource entries is a couple of kilobytes; anything far larger is refused before any decoding is spent on it.

<a id="limes.MaxLeeway"></a>

### limes.MaxLeeway

```go
const MaxLeeway = 5 * time.Minute
```

MaxLeeway is the widest VerifierConfig.Leeway a verifier takes: a token is accepted for at most this long past its expiry, which is what lets a store purge it safely after MinPurgeRetention.

<sub>[verifier.go](../../verifier.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.ErrAuthSchemeMismatch"></a>

### limes.ErrAuthSchemeMismatch

```go
var ErrAuthSchemeMismatch error = &familyError{"limes: token presented under the wrong scheme", ErrProofOfPossession}
```

ErrAuthSchemeMismatch — the scheme the token came under is not the one its binding calls for: a key-bound token as Bearer, which RFC 9449 §7.2 treats as a downgrade, or an unbound one as DPoP. Matches ErrProofOfPossession: the binding, not the token, is what the scheme fails.

<sub>[authorization.go](../../authorization.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.ErrMalformedAuthorization"></a>

### limes.ErrMalformedAuthorization

```go
var ErrMalformedAuthorization error = &familyError{"limes: malformed Authorization header", ErrInvalidRequest}
```

ErrMalformedAuthorization — an Authorization header that is not one scheme this module reads followed by one token68 credential. It is a malformed request (RFC 6750 §3.1 invalid\_request), not a bad token, so it matches ErrInvalidRequest; ErrorResponse still answers it 400, as the client's fault, where the rest of that family is the server's own call.

<sub>[authorization.go](../../authorization.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.ErrNoCredentials"></a>

### limes.ErrNoCredentials

```go
var ErrNoCredentials error = &familyError{"limes: no credentials", ErrUnauthenticated}
```

ErrNoCredentials — the request carries no credential this module reads: no Authorization header, or one under a scheme other than Bearer or DPoP. RFC 6750 §3.1 answers it with a challenge and no error code: the client has not tried, so nothing it sent was wrong.

<sub>[authorization.go](../../authorization.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.AuthSchemeUnspecified"></a><a id="limes.AuthSchemeBearer"></a><a id="limes.AuthSchemeDPoP"></a>

#### limes.AuthSchemeUnspecified, limes.AuthSchemeBearer, limes.AuthSchemeDPoP

```go
const (
	// AuthSchemeUnspecified is a token that did not come from an
	// Authorization header — a gRPC metadata entry, a message field.
	// Verify checks no scheme for it (VerifyRequest.Scheme); a key-bound
	// token still needs its DPoP proof.
	AuthSchemeUnspecified AuthScheme = ""
	// AuthSchemeBearer presents a bearer token (RFC 6750).
	AuthSchemeBearer AuthScheme = "Bearer"
	// AuthSchemeDPoP presents a key-bound token (RFC 9449 §7.1).
	AuthSchemeDPoP AuthScheme = "DPoP"
)
```

<sub>[authorization.go](../../authorization.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.ParseAuthorization"></a>

#### limes.ParseAuthorization

```go
func ParseAuthorization(header string) (AuthScheme, string, error)
```

ParseAuthorization reads an Authorization header value: the scheme, matched without regard to case (RFC 9110 §11.1), and its token68 credential. With ErrMalformedAuthorization it still returns the scheme it recognised, so ErrorResponse challenges under the scheme the client used.

<sub>[authorization.go](../../authorization.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.ParseAuthorizationValues"></a>

#### limes.ParseAuthorizationValues

```go
func ParseAuthorizationValues(values []string) (AuthScheme, string, error)
```

ParseAuthorizationValues reads every Authorization field a request carries — r.Header.Values(AuthorizationHeader), or a gRPC metadata entry's values — as ParseAuthorization reads one. More than one is ErrMalformedAuthorization, with no scheme: RFC 9449 §7.2 refuses a request that uses more than one authentication method, and RFC 6750 §2 one that presents a token more than once, so none of them is chosen. None is ErrNoCredentials.

type BiscuitConfig struct {
	// Revocations answers whether a copy of a Biscuit is revoked on its
	// own. Required; wrap the store in the RevocationCache that
	// VerifierConfig.Revocations holds, with RevocationCacheConfig.Biscuits
	// set. NewVerifier refuses a *RevocationCache without it, or a nil one;

	// copies a MeterSubject carries; off, such a token is refused with

<a id="limes.KeyResolver"></a>

### limes.KeyResolver

```go
type KeyResolver interface {
	// PublicKey returns the Ed25519 public key for the given kid.
	// Returns jwks.ErrUnknownKID if the key set does not contain the kid,
	// which the verifier reads as the token's fault (ErrInvalidToken).
	// Any other error is the resolver's: the verifier refuses the token
	// with it as it is, the server's fault rather than the token's.
	PublicKey(ctx context.Context, kid string) (ed25519.PublicKey, error)
}
```

KeyResolver resolves a JWKS \`kid\` to the public key the verifier should use. jwks.Static holds keys in memory; jwks.Remote fetches them from an issuer's JWKS endpoint with a cache.

Keys are Ed25519 for all of 1.x: the token format, not the key, names the algorithm, so another algorithm would be another format (limes\_v) rather than a key this interface returns.

<a id="limes.Verifier"></a>

### limes.Verifier

```go
type Verifier struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Verifier is the production verifier — signature first, then claims, then issuer / tenant / time / audience / revocation gates. A deployment typically resolves keys through a cached JWKS (jwks.Remote) and checks revocation through a short-TTL cache (RevocationCache), so revocation propagates quickly without hammering the store. A consumer that mocks it declares the narrow interface it needs.

Verification is independent of the persistence layer apart from the revocation lookup, so the verifier scales horizontally without contention on the capability records.

<sub>[verifier.go](../../verifier.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.Verifier.Authorize"></a>

#### limes.Verifier.Authorize

```go
func (v *Verifier) Authorize(ctx context.Context, req AuthorizeRequest) (VerifiedCapability, error)
```

Authorize is Verify followed by every caveat that can be checked without state: the operation, the resource, the idempotency key, the tainted read (Caveats.Check), and the client's address (Caveats.CheckSource). The request and budget limits are stateful: a meter.Meter enforces them, through Bump and Charge, inside the consumer's own transaction. The caveats are checked before the proof's id is recorded, so a presenter they refuse — one outside the allowed networks, say — spends none of the replay cache's room, which every holder of the capability shares.

<sub>[verifier.go](../../verifier.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.Verifier.BiscuitCopy"></a>

#### limes.Verifier.BiscuitCopy

```go
func (v *Verifier) BiscuitCopy(ctx context.Context, token string) (BiscuitCopy, error)
```

BiscuitCopy reads which copy token is, after checking it as Verify does — the sealed token's signature, issuer and tenant, then the Biscuit's signature chain — so that a revocation is only ever recorded against a capability the token genuinely carries. A token that is not a Biscuit, is longer than VerifierConfig.MaxTokenBytes, or comes to a verifier with no VerifierConfig.Biscuit is ErrInvalidToken. Expiry, audience and revocation are not checked: a copy can be revoked whatever its state. Nor is BiscuitConfig.MeterCopies: a copy carrying limits is named, and can be revoked, on any verifier.

<sub>[verifier.go](../../verifier.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.Verifier.ErrorResponse"></a>

#### limes.Verifier.ErrorResponse

```go
func (v *Verifier) ErrorResponse(ctx context.Context, err error, scheme AuthScheme) ErrorResponse
```

ErrorResponse is how to answer a request refused with err, presented under scheme. A refusal about the token is challenged under the scheme the client used (Bearer when it named none); one about the proof, under DPoP. A verifier with DPoP configured also advertises its algorithms in a DPoP challenge, and hands out a fresh nonce with use\_dpop\_nonce; when it cannot give one, it logs why (VerifierConfig.Logger) and answers the server's failure, 500, for a challenge without a nonce is one the client cannot satisfy. An error it has no answer for — ErrInvalidRequest's family but ErrMalformedAuthorization, ErrNotFound, a store's own failure — is answered 500, without its text.

<sub>[challenge.go](../../challenge.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.Verifier.Introspect"></a>

#### limes.Verifier.Introspect

```go
func (v *Verifier) Introspect(ctx context.Context, token string) (Introspection, error)
```

Introspect answers an introspection endpoint (RFC 7662) about a token a resource server or gateway holds a copy of: nil error if it is active — genuine, from a trusted issuer, within its time window and not revoked, itself, through an ancestor or, for a Biscuit, through a copy — with the capability it carries. It checks neither an audience nor proof of possession: a key-bound token is active though no key was proved, and the answer says the token is bound, not that its presenter holds the key. A token lifted out of the Biscuit it was sealed in is refused, as Verify refuses it. So is a Biscuit copy that sets request or budget limits of its own, on a verifier without BiscuitConfig.MeterCopies: ErrCopyCountersNotMetered, as Verify answers it; with MeterCopies, the answer carries those limits in Introspection.Copies. A refusal of the token is ErrUnauthenticated's family, which the endpoint answers as inactive; any other error is the server's, such as a revocation lookup that failed, and never reads as inactive.

Introspect is no authorization: it yields no VerifiedCapability, so its answer can be neither delegated from nor checked against a request.

Introspect answers about a token of any audience. An endpoint whose callers may each learn only about tokens of some audiences uses IntrospectFor, which refuses any other token before the revocation lookup.

<sub>[verifier.go](../../verifier.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.Verifier.IntrospectFor"></a>

#### limes.Verifier.IntrospectFor

```go
func (v *Verifier) IntrospectFor(ctx context.Context, req IntrospectRequest) (Introspection, error)
```

IntrospectFor is Introspect for a caller that may learn only about tokens of req.Audiences. A token whose audience names none of them is refused as ErrAudienceMismatch once its signatures, issuer and time window have verified, and before the revocation lookup: so a foreign token is refused alike whether the revocation store can answer or not, and a forged one is refused as ever, both as ErrUnauthenticated's family. A token of an audience the caller may ask about is answered as Introspect answers it, a revocation lookup that failed included.

<sub>[verifier.go](../../verifier.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.Verifier.Verify"></a>

#### limes.Verifier.Verify

```go
func (v *Verifier) Verify(ctx context.Context, req VerifyRequest) (VerifiedCapability, error)
```

Verify checks the token itself: its signature, issuer and tenant, its validity window, its audience, the proof of possession a key-bound capability needs, and revocation. It returns the capability the token grants; a refusal is one of the package's sentinels, so the caller can branch on the failure mode.

Order matters: nothing in the claims is read until the signature over them has verified, so a forged JWT costs a header decode and one signature check, and no claim-parsing path is reachable by an attacker. A Biscuit is read further before its signatures are checked: its container and every block are decoded and their facts read as data, which MaxTokenBytes and MaxBiscuitBlocks bound; none of it is trusted until the signatures have verified. The checks that need no I/O come before the revocation lookup — the proof of possession among them, so a holder of a key-bound token without its key learns nothing of the token's revocation and causes no lookup — and the proof's id is recorded in the replay cache last, so neither a revoked token nor a copy this verifier cannot meter records one.

<sub>[verifier.go](../../verifier.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.VerifierConfig"></a>

### limes.VerifierConfig

```go
type VerifierConfig struct {
	// Keys resolves JWKS kids to Ed25519 public keys.
	Keys KeyResolver

	// Revocations answers whether a capability — or any ancestor in its
	// delegation chain — is revoked. Wrap the store in a
	// RevocationCache to keep the per-call cost flat.
	//
	// It must see the records of every issuer in TrustedIssuers: a
	// capability it has no record of reads as not revoked (IsRevoked), so
	// one whose issuer records elsewhere — another store, a tenant the
	// lookup's role cannot see, rows a restore from backup lost — verifies
	// and can never be revoked. Such a capability is refused unless
	// AllowUnrecorded is set.
	Revocations RevocationLookup

	// AllowUnrecorded reads a capability Revocations has no record of as
	// not revoked. Unset — the default — such a capability is refused with
	// ErrUnrecorded, a Biscuit's capability as a JWT's: a lookup that
	// cannot see a record could not see its revocation either.
	// Revocations must then tell the two apart: a RevocationLineageLookup,
	// as memstore's and pgstore's Store are, or a RevocationCache over one;
	// NewVerifier refuses any other with ErrInvalidConfig unless
	// AllowUnrecorded is set. A type of yours that wraps a cache is seen as
	// the RevocationLineageLookup it is: one forwarding RevocationLineage to
	// the cache keeps the check, and over a cache whose upstream names no
	// lineage every verification fails with ErrNoRevocationLineage, never
	// passes. A RevocationLineageLookup that answers an id not on record as
	// not revoked, against its contract, defeats the check unseen.
	//
	// The trade-off is replica lag. An Issuer returns a token only once its
	// record is written, so only a lookup that reads a lagging replica
	// misses one: a fresh token is refused, as ErrUnrecorded (401, not
	// permanent), until replication brings its record there, and a
	// RevocationCache keeps that answer for its TTL. Set AllowUnrecorded to
	// accept such tokens instead, at the cost of accepting, unrevocably, a
	// token whose record the lookup never sees.
	AllowUnrecorded bool

	// TrustedIssuers is the set of issuer values the verifier accepts.
	// Tokens whose `iss` claim is not in the set are rejected with
	// ErrInvalidToken.
	TrustedIssuers []string

	// KeyIssuers binds each kid to the one issuer allowed to sign with it:
	// a token whose kid is absent from the map, or whose `iss` differs from
	// the kid's binding, is rejected. Empty binds no kid: enough with one
	// trusted issuer. With several it is required, unless SharedKeys says
	// otherwise: any trusted key signing for any trusted issuer is wrong for
	// issuers that do not share a trust boundary, so it is never the default.
	// One key signs for two issuers — a family of capabilities marked by
	// an iss of its own — under two kids, each bound here to its issuer:
	// two Issuers with the same key, each with its kid and IssuerName.
	// SharedKeys would let any trusted key sign either iss, which defeats
	// the mark.
	KeyIssuers map[string]string

	// SharedKeys lets every trusted key sign for every trusted issuer, for
	// several issuers that do share one trust boundary. It and KeyIssuers
	// exclude each other.
	SharedKeys bool

	// Now is the time function the verifier uses for nbf/exp. Nil:
	// time.Now.
	Now func() time.Time

	// Leeway widens the nbf / exp window to absorb clock skew between
	// issuer and verifier. Zero: DefaultLeeway; negative or past MaxLeeway
	// is refused.
	Leeway time.Duration
	// NoLeeway holds nbf and exp to the verifier's clock exactly, for an
	// issuer that shares it. It excludes a Leeway.
	NoLeeway bool

	// MaxTokenBytes rejects longer tokens before decoding them. Default
	// DefaultMaxTokenBytes when zero; negative is refused.
	MaxTokenBytes int

	// Biscuit accepts the Biscuit form (Issuer.Biscuit, biscuit.Attenuate)
	// beside the JWT, as it says. Nil: a Biscuit is refused like any
	// malformed token.
	Biscuit *BiscuitConfig

	// DPoP checks the proof of possession a key-bound capability (one with
	// a ConfirmationJKT) must come with. Without it the verifier refuses
	// every key-bound capability with ErrProofUnsupported, rather than accept
	// one as a bearer token. Built by dpop.NewVerifier, with its own clock.
	DPoP *dpop.Verifier

	// Realm names the protection space in every WWW-Authenticate challenge
	// ErrorResponse gives (RFC 9110 §11.5). Empty: DefaultRealm. Only the
	// characters RFC 6750 §3 allows in an auth-param value.
	Realm string

	// Logger logs every token checked, by Verify, Authorize, Introspect and
	// BiscuitCopy, naming the capability by id, issuer and kid and never
	// logging a token or a proof. The levels follow who can cause the line:
	// a token accepted at DEBUG; a token refused after its signature
	// verified — expired, revoked, unrecorded, for another audience, without
	// its proof, outside its caveats — at WARN, since only a holder of a
	// genuine token causes it; a token refused before — absent, malformed,
	// forged, under an unknown kid — at DEBUG, since anyone can send one in
	// volume; a check that failed for the server's own reasons — the keys or
	// the revocations out of reach — at ERROR. It also logs what
	// ErrorResponse cannot answer the way the refusal asks: a nonce the DPoP
	// verifier cannot give. Nil: slog.Default().
	Logger *slog.Logger

	// Events are called beside the log, for metrics or an audit sink. The
	// zero VerifierEvents calls nothing.
	Events VerifierEvents
}
```

VerifierConfig wires the verifier. Keys, Revocations and TrustedIssuers are required.

<sub>[verifier.go](../../verifier.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.VerifyRequest"></a>

### limes.VerifyRequest

```go
type VerifyRequest struct {
	// Token is the capability token, a JWT or a Biscuit. Empty is
	// ErrNoCredentials.
	Token string
	// Audience is the service the call is hitting: the token's audience
	// must include it. Required: empty is ErrInvalidRequest, the server's
	// error rather than the token's.
	Audience string
	// DPoP is the request's proof of possession, needed when the
	// capability is key-bound and ignored when it is not.
	DPoP dpop.Proof
	// Scheme is the Authorization scheme the token came under
	// (ParseAuthorization). Set, it must match the binding: DPoP for a
	// key-bound capability, Bearer for any other.
	Scheme AuthScheme
}
```

VerifyRequest is a token as it arrived, and what it arrived for.
